name: EXACT-BARYCENTRIC-INTERPOLATE

primary_sources.authority: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions
primary_sources.scope: unique interpolation polynomial through pairwise distinct nodes
barycentric interpolation representation and distinct-node algorithm

law: Given 1..n pairwise-distinct exact rational node abscissas x_i and exact rational ordinates y_i, and exact rational query x, return the unique exact rational value of polynomial degree at most n−1 interpolating all nodes (x_i,y_i). Evaluate at x_i exactly y_i, reject duplicate x_i, empty set and inexact values; permutation of nodes must not alter result. Evaluate by barycentric rational weights, not floating coefficients.
formula: If x=x_i return y_i. Otherwise w_i=1/product_{j≠i}(x_i−x_j) and p(x)=(sum_i w_i*y_i/(x−x_i))/(sum_i w_i/(x−x_i)).
falsifiers: Return a rounded float 0.25 rather than exact rational 1/4 on exact nodes/query.
Silently accept repeated x_i with inconsistent y_i, giving division by zero or arbitrary output.
Return interpolated coefficients rather than evaluated exact p(x), violating the declared result type.
Change result when reversing the node list, or produce a value other than y_i at an interpolation node.
Conflate polynomial interpolation with band-limited SDR reconstruction, sensor uncertainty propagation, hardware timing, or physical ephemeris accuracy.

closest_existing: D10 SDR and generic sequence constructors
dedup.semantic_difference: Interpolation through multiple exact samples is not constrained-denominator approximation of one rational. Despite distinct observable behavior, it is derivable from arithmetic and finite folds.
